The most recent source I found is Neon's own blog, which says the Free plan now gives **1 GB of storage per project** (up from 0.5 GB) and still allows **100 projects**. Other pages still list 0.5 GB, so they may be out of date.

- **Projects:** 100 total on the Free plan, per Neon's FAQ. The Neon Free plan costs $0/month and includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month, 0.5 GB of storage per project, and 5 GB of public network transfer per project per month.
- **Compute:** The 100 CU-hours are per project and reset monthly. Compute scales to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity and can scale up to 2 CU (≈8 GB RAM) when active.
- **Storage:** The blog reports 1 GB per project. Its earlier 0.5 GB figure appears in the FAQ and pricing pages. Storage limits apply continuously rather than monthly.
- **Branches:** 10 per project. Extra child branches are not available on Free.
- **Hitting a limit:** Compute is suspended when CU-hours or network transfer run out, and suspension doesn't delete data. Exceeding storage also suspends the project rather than billing you.

**Conflicts:** A pricing-plans page in the results says Free has 50 CU-hours/project, 0.5 GB storage per branch, which contradicts the 100 CU-hours figure elsewhere. A third-party article lists 10 projects instead of 100, and it's probably outdated. The Neon FAQ and pricing page both give 100 CU-hours, so I'd trust those over the 50-hour figure. Check neon.com/pricing for the current numbers.

## Free tiers for Postgres: Neon, Supabase and PlanetScale

I couldn't open the vendors' pricing pages directly, because the fetch tool's proxy refused the connection. Everything below comes from search-result summaries. Please check the official pages before relying on any number.

| | **Neon (Free)** | **Supabase (Free)** | **PlanetScale** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier? | Yes, $0/month | Yes | Most likely no (see below) |
| Projects | 100 | 2 active | n/a |
| Storage | 0.5 GB per project on the FAQ and pricing pages. A Neon blog post says 1 GB per project. | 500 MB database size, plus 1 GB file storage | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month. Scales to zero after 5 minutes idle, up to 2 CU (about 8 GB RAM). | Not found | n/a |
| Network | 5 GB public transfer per project per month | 5 GB egress | n/a |
| Branches | 10 per project | Not found | n/a |
| Other | Compute suspends at the limits, and data isn't deleted. | 50,000 monthly active users. Projects pause after 1 week of inactivity. | Cheapest paid option is $5/month |

**Neon**
- The 100 projects, 10 branches, 100 CU-hours, 5 GB transfer and the 5-minute scale-to-zero all come from Neon's [Free plan FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas) and [pricing page](https://neon.com/pricing).
- The 1 GB per project figure comes from a [Neon blog post](https://neon.com/blog/neon-free-plan-1-gb-per-project). It is the most recent source I found, so the 0.5 GB figure may be out of date.
- A plans page in the results listed 50 CU-hours and storage per branch. That conflicts with the FAQ and pricing page, so I went with their 100 CU-hours.
- A third-party article says 10 projects, which is probably stale.

**Supabase**
- The 500 MB database, 5 GB egress, 2 active projects and the 1-week pause come from [Supabase's pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing.md).
- The 1 GB file storage and 50,000 monthly active users come from third-party guides that agree with each other, such as [Jetadmin](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/supabase-pricing-2026-guide-to-plans-limits-and-real-world-costs/).
- One third-party table says 2 GB egress. I used the official 5 GB.
- A paused project keeps its data, but you have to restore it manually from the dashboard. This is also from a third-party guide.

**PlanetScale**
- PlanetScale removed its free Hobby plan in April 2024, and most sources say it hasn't come back.
- It added Postgres with a Base plan from $5/month, which is a single-node, non-HA database. This is from a [Bytebase comparison](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/) and other third-party sources.
- One [CostBench page](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/) claims a free plan exists as of June 2026. Other pages on the same site contradict it, so I don't trust it.
- I never reached PlanetScale's own pricing page, so "no free tier" is my best reading of the evidence, not a confirmed fact.

**Summary:** Neon has the most generous free Postgres, with many projects and scale-to-zero. Supabase gives you only 2 projects, and they pause after a week of inactivity, but it includes auth, file storage and an API. PlanetScale appears to be paid-only for Postgres.

Sources:
- [Neon free plan FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas)
- [Neon pricing](https://neon.com/pricing)
- [Neon blog: 1 GB per project](https://neon.com/blog/neon-free-plan-1-gb-per-project)
- [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing.md)
- [Jetadmin: Supabase pricing guide](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/supabase-pricing-2026-guide-to-plans-limits-and-real-world-costs/)
- [Bytebase: Postgres hosting pricing comparison](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/)
- [CostBench: PlanetScale free plan](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/)
